status: DESIGN RECORD: untested hypothesis. No cell, no seed, no threshold, no bar.
hypothesis: sparse-world geometry: selection precision depends on the density of true edges in the candidate universe, not only on the selection rule
not_evidence: docs/DECAY-FIX-CONFIRMATION-PREREGISTRATION.md section 18: that campaign held world geometry fixed and varied only the threshold, so it says nothing about density
no result in this repository varies density as a manipulation

world_pairs.definition: P_world = directed non-self tag pairs of the world's own vocabulary
world_pairs.role: the oracle-filtered universe; |W|/|P_world| is a property of the world

rank_population.definition: P_rank = the rows the ranker can actually select from at the end of a run: intra-cell co-occurrence rows, sleep-sourced pairs, and any pair over the world vocabulary the engine holds
rank_population.role: produced by the frozen engine, so it is measured per cell, never set
rank_population.note: |W|/|P_world| and |W and P_rank|/|P_rank| are different ratios and can move in different directions; a design that reports only the first reports a world property as if it were the ranker's difficulty

density.note: counts and densities are different manipulations: 500 true edges is impossible at 16 tags, because |P_world| is 240

counts_are_not_densities.note: a 500-edge world needs at least 23 tags and is then 0.988 dense, not a denser version of the 16-tag world

exposure.primary: fixed total exposure: the same events and cycles at every density, so each edge is observed fewer times as density rises
exposure.sensitivity: fixed exposure per edge: cycles scale with |W|, so the curriculum length varies with density
exposure.confound_rule: a density effect that reverses under the other exposure scheme is an exposure artifact, not geometry

comparison.design: at each density, the same ranking intervention and its control, differing only in the selection rule
comparison.claim: the intervention's benefit depends on density iff Delta varies with density
not_claimed: a main effect of density is not an interaction
an interaction does not show that density caused any earlier failure

confounds_to_hold.vocabulary: fix the tag count, so |C| and every source-frequency denominator stay fixed; adding tags to reach higher edge counts is a separate arm and is never pooled with the fixed-vocabulary ladder
confounds_to_hold.world_family: one generator; a second family is a separate arm
confounds_to_hold.horizon: the primary scheme fixes it; the sensitivity scheme reports its own

evidence: all 112 true world edges were present in memory in the Gate 13 world, so presence was never the binding constraint
under global count-ranked selection the top 20 recovered 0-1 of 112 in the three-seed table and 0-3 of 112 in the five-seed capacity sweep
cap 40 recovered 1-8 of 112; top 320, about 16x the engine's budget, recovered 106-109
ranking_bottleneck.ceiling_caveat: 0.3438 is the maximum precision observed for the tested frequency-based allocation rules and budgets in that world family; it is not an information-theoretic bound and must not be quoted as the ceiling of what any selection could achieve

endpoints: presence ceiling: |W available in memory| / |W|; must be 1.0 or the cell tests memory
precision: |asserted and W| / |asserted|, reported with rho_rank
interaction: Delta(rho) across density levels, with a paired interval on the difference of differences
falsifier: Delta(d) flat in density falsifies the claim that geometry is the lever for this ranking bottleneck; it does not falsify density as a factor elsewhere

allocation.note: this record allocates nothing; a pre-registration with fresh seeds comes first, per docs/DECAY-TUNING-CYCLE.md

control.name: global count-ranked top-k
control.rule: the engine's own selection: rank every candidate by count and take the top k at the frozen cap

treatment.name: intra-cell-excluded ranking
treatment.rule: identical cap, identical scoring, identical admission window; intra-cell co-occurrence rows are simply not eligible for the top-k

identical_by_construction: candidate generation, the cap, the scoring function and the admission window
the world, the seed, the exposure scheme and the horizon at each density level
treatment.mechanism_claim: the intervention changes only what may occupy the budget, so any gain is budget competition, not a better score
treatment.why_this_one: Gate 13 measured the top-20 as 75-100% intra-cell, so a row class that cannot be a world edge was occupying budget that world edges needed

predictions: the control's top-k precision rises with rho_world, mechanically, because the population it samples is denser; this is predicted and is not the claim
Delta(rho) = treated - control declines as rho_world rises
the advantage is largest at the lowest density, where control coverage is near zero
predicted_direction.limit: as rho_world approaches 1 every candidate is a true edge, the two arms select the same rows, and Delta must go to 0; a non-zero Delta there is a harness defect
falsifiers: Delta flat in rho: geometry is not the lever for this ranking bottleneck
Delta rising in rho: the mechanism claim is wrong and something other than budget competition is being measured
Delta non-zero at rho_world = 1: the arms are not identical where they must be

analysis_rules: axis liveness: rho_rank must move with rho_world, or the manipulation did not reach the ranker and the cells measure nothing

precision cannot exceed min(1, |W and P_rank| / k): a k-row selection cannot contain more world rows than the pool holds. It is NOT bounded by rho_rank -- a ranker that prefers world rows can exceed it, measured at 1.000 against 0.800 in the density review (2026-11-07). Every precision figure is reported beside rho_rank and the budget it was measured at
coverage is reported with its denominator |W|, because a denser world makes the same selection cover less of a larger W
recovery is reported as a distribution across budgets, never as the rank of the first edge

amendments.direction: at a fixed cap, the treatment's advantage rises with rho_world; the advantage is largest at the dense end
amendments.why: the benefit of freeing budget is bounded by how many world rows exist to fill it, and that count grows with density: a sparse world has too few world edges for the freed budget to spend on. The original prediction reasoned from coverage's denominator (small |W|, large relative gain) to a claim about a fixed budget
amendments.evidence: docs/density_interaction_prereg.json, leverage_audit: on the designed pools over the registered seeds the advantage is 0.075 at rho_world 0.1 and 0.350 at 0.8
amendments.consequence: 'rising' is no longer a falsifier of the claim; it is the claim, and the registration carries its own falsifiers (flat, or falling)
